summary.value: The Chantecler is the only chicken breed that comes from Canada. Brother Wilfrid Chatelain, a monk at the abbey in Oka, Quebec, started work on it in 1908 and showed it to the public in 1918. He wanted a sturdy farm bird that could handle Canadian winters, so the breed has tight, dense feathers, a tiny cushion comb and almost no wattles, which keeps frostbite away. White is the original color, and a partridge version came later from Alberta. Roosters weigh about 7.5 to 8.5 pounds and hens about 5.5 pounds. Hens lay around 200 to 220 large light brown eggs a year and keep laying in winter. They are gentle, calm birds that grow friendly when handled young, and some hens go broody. The breed is rare today. It is a strong pick for cold northern climates but does poorly in hot weather.
